tldr: Existing heuristic multimodal RAG methods suffer from rigid retrieval processes that fail on dynamic questions; the authors propose Dyn-VQA, a dataset of 1,452 complex dynamic questions, and OmniSearch, a self-adaptive retrieval planning agent that significantly outperforms existing methods.
contributions: Propose Dyn-VQA, a dataset of 1,452 dynamic questions spanning three types: rapidly changing answers, multi-modal knowledge requirements, and multi-hop reasoning.
Benchmark various mRAG methods with leading MLLMs on Dyn-VQA, demonstrating their flaws in handling dynamic questions.
Propose OmniSearch, the first self-adaptive multimodal retrieval agent that dynamically decomposes complex questions into sub-question chains with retrieval actions.
Show through extensive experiments that OmniSearch (GPT-4V) significantly outperforms state-of-the-art MLLMs with heuristic mRAGs and commercial generative search engines.
methods: The authors constructed Dyn-VQA through a three-step annotation process: textual question writing categorized by answer update frequency, modality, and reasoning hops; multimodal rewriting replacing visual concepts with co-references paired with real images; and Chinese-English translation with manual verification. They then proposed OmniSearch, a self-adaptive planning agent consisting of three modules: a planning agent that decomposes questions into sub-questions and plans retrieval actions (self-thought, sub-question, retrieval API, and query), a retriever executing web/image searches, and a sub-question solver generating feedback. Two versions were developed based on GPT-4V and Qwen-VL-Chat, with the latter trained using a retrieval API dataset synthesized from GPT-4V and Infoseek.
results: OmniSearch (GPT-4V) significantly outperforms other models including state-of-the-art MLLMs with heuristic mRAGs and commercial generative search engines. Even Qwen-VL-Chat-based OmniSearch surpasses considerably larger GPT-4V equipped with two-step heuristic mRAG. Commercial generative search engines perform poorly, with best-performing Gemini only matching GPT-4V with two-step mRAG. Using GPT-4V as sub-question solver significantly enhances Qwen-VL-Chat-based OmniSearch performance. Despite achieving more than 50% performance, Dyn-VQA remains formidable, with fast-changing, >2-hop, and external visual knowledge questions posing the most intractable challenges.
limitations: Significant gap remains between OmniSearch and human performance on the three most challenging subcategories (fast-changing, >2-hop, requiring external visual knowledge).
Retriever tools are limited to web search, image search with text, and image retrieval with images.
Questions requiring rapidly changing knowledge pose the most intractable challenge as such knowledge cannot be internalized by MLLMs.
All models consistently underperform on questions necessitating multi-step retrieval or additional visual knowledge.
